fullText.simplified:
第二章、我写《橘颂》

    公元前340年，我出生了，我是楚国人。
    当时楚国有三大家族，他们是楚国最有权势的人。我家姓屈，屈家是这三大家族之一。
    我的童年是在一个叫乐平里的地方度过的。那里的百姓很好，山水很漂亮，还有各种美丽的动物和植物。我从小就爱读书，什么书都读。我经常拿着书行走在山水之间，一边读书，一边看那些有趣的植物和动物。有时遇到出门种地的人们，他们会笑着问我，是书有意思还是花花草草有意思。那是一个快乐的童年。
    我的家乡有一种甜美多汁的水果，叫橘子。橘子只生长在南方，出了楚国就吃不到了。我从小就爱吃橘子，我家附近有很多橘树。我经常在橘树下读书，闻着橘树和橘子的香味，觉得人生很美好。
    我给橘子写了一首诗，叫《橘颂》。我在诗中这样写道：

    “天地间的美好树木啊，生来就在南国的土地上。
    绿色的叶子白色的花朵，样子多么可爱啊。
    根在南国，生长在天地间，从来不受别人的影响。
    希望与你一起长大，与你一直做朋友啊。
    ……”

    《橘颂》是中国第一首“借物言志”的诗歌，也是后人认识我的起点。后人都说我像橘树，深爱国家，诚实专一。但说实话，写诗的时候我没有想这么多，因为那时候我还年轻，没有经历苦难。
    《橘颂》流传到了楚国的首都——引都，住在那儿的王读了我的诗，表示很喜欢。二十岁时，我接到王的通知，要我去引都。
    引都是楚国最重要的城市，我去那儿是去做官的。当然，我得到做官的机会不完全是因为《橘颂》，我的父母很早就跟我说过，三大家族的孩子长大了都是要做官的。
    我收拾行李，离开了家乡。
fullText.traditional:
第二章、我寫《橘頌》

    公元前340年，我出生了，我是楚國人。
    當時楚國有三大家族，他們是楚國最有權勢的人。我家姓屈，屈家是這三大家族之一。
    我的童年是在一個叫樂平里的地方度過的。那裡的百姓很好，山水很漂亮，還有各種美麗的動物和植物。我從小就愛讀書，什麼書都讀。我經常拿著書行走在山水之間，一邊讀書，一邊看那些有趣的植物和動物。有時遇到出門種地的人們，他們會笑著問我，是書有意思還是花花草草有意思。那是一個快樂的童年。
    我的家鄉有一種甜美多汁的水果，叫橘子。橘子只生長在南方，出了楚國就吃不到了。我從小就愛吃橘子，我家附近有很多橘樹。我經常在橘樹下讀書，聞著橘樹和橘子的香味，覺得人生很美好。
    我給橘子寫了一首詩，叫《橘頌》。我在詩中這樣寫道：

    “天地間的美好樹木啊，生來就在南國的土地上。
    綠色的葉子白色的花朵，樣子多麼可愛啊。
    根在南國，生長在天地間，從來不受別人的影響。
    希望與你一起長大，與你一直做朋友啊。
    ……”

    《橘頌》是中國第一首“借物言志”的詩歌，也是後人認識我的起點。後人都說我像橘樹，深愛國家，誠實專一。但說實話，寫詩的時候我沒有想這麼多，因為那時候我還年輕，沒有經歷苦難。
    《橘頌》流傳到了楚國的首都——引都，住在那兒的王讀了我的詩，表示很喜歡。二十歲時，我接到王的通知，要我去引都。
    引都是楚國最重要的城市，我去那兒是去做官的。當然，我得到做官的機會不完全是因為《橘頌》，我的父母很早就跟我說過，三大家族的孩子長大了都是要做官的。
    我收拾行李，離開了家鄉。

sentences.simplified: 公元前340年，我出生了，我是楚国人。
sentences.traditional: 公元前340年，我出生了，我是楚國人。
sentences.pinyin: gōng yuán qián nián wǒ chū shēng le wǒ shì chǔ guó rén
sentences.english: I was born in 340 BC. I am from the state of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 当时楚国有三大家族，他们是楚国最有权势的人。
sentences.traditional: 當時楚國有三大家族，他們是楚國最有權勢的人。
sentences.pinyin: dāng shí chǔ guó yǒu sān dà jiā zú tā men shì chǔ guó zuì yǒu quán shì de rén
sentences.english: At that time, there were three great families in the state of Chu. They were the most powerful people in the state of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 我家姓屈，屈家是这三大家族之一。
sentences.traditional: 我家姓屈，屈家是這三大家族之一。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jiā xìng qū qū jiā shì zhè sān dà jiā zú zhī yī
sentences.english: My family name is Qu, and the Qu family was one of these three great families.

sentences.simplified: 我的童年是在一个叫乐平里的地方度过的。
sentences.traditional: 我的童年是在一個叫樂平里的地方度過的。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de tóng nián shì zài yí ge jiào lè píng lǐ de dì fang dù guò de
sentences.english: I spent my childhood in a place called Lepingli.

sentences.simplified: 那里的百姓很好，山水很漂亮，还有各种美丽的动物和植物。
sentences.traditional: 那裡的百姓很好，山水很漂亮，還有各種美麗的動物和植物。
sentences.pinyin: nà lǐ de bǎi xìng hěn hǎo shān shuǐ hěn piào liang hái yǒu gè zhǒng měi lì de dòng wù hé zhí wù
sentences.english: The people there were very kind, the scenery was beautiful, and there were all kinds of lovely animals and plants.

sentences.simplified: 我从小就爱读书，什么书都读。
sentences.traditional: 我從小就愛讀書，什麼書都讀。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ cóng xiǎo jiù ài dú shū shén me shū dōu dú
sentences.english: I loved reading from a young age and read all kinds of books.

sentences.simplified: 我经常拿着书行走在山水之间，一边读书，一边看那些有趣的植物和动物。
sentences.traditional: 我經常拿著書行走在山水之間，一邊讀書，一邊看那些有趣的植物和動物。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jīng cháng ná zhe shū xíng zǒu zài shān shuǐ zhī jiān yì biān dú shū yì biān kàn nà xiē yǒu qù de zhí wù hé dòng wù
sentences.english: I often walked among the mountains and rivers with a book in hand, reading as I observed the interesting plants and animals.

sentences.simplified: 有时遇到出门种地的人们，
sentences.traditional: 有時遇到出門種地的人們，
sentences.pinyin: yǒu shí yù dào chū mén zhòng dì de rén men
sentences.english: Sometimes I would meet people going out to work in the fields, ..

sentences.traditional: 他們會笑著問我，是書有意思還是花花草草有意思。

sentences.english: .. and they would smile and ask me whether it was the books that were interesting, or the flowers and plants that were interesting.

sentences.simplified: 那是一个快乐的童年。
sentences.traditional: 那是一個快樂的童年。
sentences.pinyin: nà shì yí ge kuài lè de tóng nián
sentences.english: It was a happy childhood.

sentences.simplified: 我的家乡有一种甜美多汁的水果，叫橘子。
sentences.traditional: 我的家鄉有一種甜美多汁的水果，叫橘子。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de jiā xiāng yǒu yì zhǒng tián měi duō zhī de shuǐ guǒ jiào jú zi
sentences.english: In my hometown, there was a sweet and juicy fruit called the orange.

sentences.traditional: 橘子只生長在南方，出了楚國就吃不到了。

sentences.english: Oranges only grew in the south, and you couldn’t find them outside the state of Chu.

sentences.simplified: 我从小就爱吃橘子，我家附近有很多橘树。
sentences.traditional: 我從小就愛吃橘子，我家附近有很多橘樹。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ cóng xiǎo jiù ài chī jú zi wǒ jiā fù jìn yǒu hěn duō jú shù
sentences.english: I loved eating oranges since I was young, and there were many orange trees near my home.

sentences.simplified: 我经常在橘树下读书，闻着橘树和橘子的香味，觉得人生很美好。
sentences.traditional: 我經常在橘樹下讀書，聞著橘樹和橘子的香味，覺得人生很美好。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ jīng cháng zài jú shù xià dú shū wén zhe jú shù hé jú zi de xiāng wèi jué de rén shēng hěn měi hǎo
sentences.english: I often read under the orange trees, and as I smelled their fragrance and that of the oranges, I felt that life was beautiful.

sentences.simplified: 我给橘子写了一首诗，叫《橘颂》。我在诗中这样写道：
sentences.traditional: 我給橘子寫了一首詩，叫《橘頌》。我在詩中這樣寫道：
sentences.pinyin: wǒ gěi jú zi xiě le yì shǒu shī jiào jú sòng wǒ zài shī zhōng zhè yàng xiě dào
sentences.english: I wrote a poem for the orange, called “Ode to the Orange Tree”. In the poem, I wrote:

sentences.simplified: “天地间的美好树木啊，生来就在南国的土地上。
sentences.traditional: “天地間的美好樹木啊，生來就在南國的土地上。
sentences.pinyin: tiān dì jiān de měi hǎo shù mù a shēng lái jiù zài nán guó de tǔ dì shang
sentences.english: “Oh, beautiful tree growing between heaven and earth, born in the lands of the southern country.

sentences.simplified: 绿色的叶子白色的花朵，样子多么可爱啊。
sentences.traditional: 綠色的葉子白色的花朵，樣子多麼可愛啊。
sentences.pinyin: lǜ sè de yè zi bái sè de huā duǒ yàng zi duō me kě ài a
sentences.english: Green leaves, white flowers—how adorable they are!

sentences.simplified: 根在南国，生长在天地间，从来不受别人的影响。
sentences.traditional: 根在南國，生長在天地間，從來不受別人的影響。
sentences.pinyin: gēn zài nán guó shēng zhǎng zài tiān dì jiān cóng lái bú shòu bié rén de yǐng xiǎng
sentences.english: Rooted in the southern country, it grows between heaven and earth, never influenced by others.

sentences.simplified: 希望与你一起长大，与你一直做朋友啊。
sentences.traditional: 希望與你一起長大，與你一直做朋友啊。
sentences.pinyin: xī wàng yǔ nǐ yì qǐ zhǎng dà yǔ nǐ yì zhí zuò péng you a
sentences.english: I hope to grow with you and always be friends with you.

sentences.simplified: 《橘颂》是中国第一首“借物言志”的诗歌，
sentences.traditional: 《橘頌》是中國第一首“借物言志”的詩歌，
sentences.pinyin: jú sòng shì zhōng guó dì yī shǒu jiè wù yán zhì de shī gē
sentences.english: “Ode to the Orange Tree” was the first Chinese poem to use an object to express the poet’s aspirations, ..

sentences.simplified: 也是后人认识我的起点。
sentences.traditional: 也是後人認識我的起點。
sentences.pinyin: yě shì hòu rén rèn shi wǒ de qǐ diǎn
sentences.english: .. and it was also how later generations started to get to know me.

sentences.simplified: 后人都说我像橘树，深爱国家，诚实专一。
sentences.traditional: 後人都說我像橘樹，深愛國家，誠實專一。
sentences.pinyin: hòu rén dōu shuō wǒ xiàng jú shù shēn ài guó jiā chéng shí zhuān yī
sentences.english: Later generations said I was like the orange tree: I had a deep love for my country, and was honest and dedicated.

sentences.simplified: 但说实话，写诗的时候我没有想这么多，因为那时候我还年轻，没有经历苦难。
sentences.traditional: 但說實話，寫詩的時候我沒有想這麼多，因為那時候我還年輕，沒有經歷苦難。
sentences.pinyin: dàn shuō shí huà xiě shī de shí hou wǒ méi yǒu xiǎng zhè me duō yīn wèi nà shí hou wǒ hái nián qīng méi yǒu jīng lì kǔ nàn
sentences.english: But to be honest, when I wrote the poem, I didn’t think that much, because I was still young and had not yet experienced hardship.

sentences.simplified: 《橘颂》流传到了楚国的首都——引都，住在那儿的王读了我的诗，表示很喜欢。
sentences.traditional: 《橘頌》流傳到了楚國的首都——引都，住在那兒的王讀了我的詩，表示很喜歡。
sentences.pinyin: jú sòng liú chuán dào le chǔ guó de shǒu dū yǐn dū zhù zài nà'r de wáng dú le wǒ de shī biǎo shì hěn xǐ huan
sentences.english: “Ode to the Orange Tree” spread to the capital of Chu—Yindu. The king living there read my poem and said that he liked it.

sentences.simplified: 二十岁时，我接到王的通知，要我去引都。
sentences.traditional: 二十歲時，我接到王的通知，要我去引都。
sentences.pinyin: èr shí suì shí wǒ jiē dào wáng de tōng zhī yào wǒ qù yǐn dū
sentences.english: At the age of twenty, I received a notice from the king asking me to go to Yindu.

sentences.simplified: 引都是楚国最重要的城市，我去那儿是去做官的。
sentences.traditional: 引都是楚國最重要的城市，我去那兒是去做官的。
sentences.pinyin: yǐn dū shì chǔ guó zuì zhòng yào de chéng shì wǒ qù nà'r shì qù zuò guān de
sentences.english: Yindu was the most important city in the state of Chu, and I went there to become an official.

sentences.simplified: 当然，我得到做官的机会不完全是因为《橘颂》，
sentences.traditional: 當然，我得到做官的機會不完全是因為《橘頌》，
sentences.pinyin: dāng rán wǒ dé dào zuò guān de jī huì bù wán quán shì yīn wèi jú sòng
sentences.english: Of course, my opportunity to become an official was not entirely because of “Ode to the Orange Tree”.

sentences.simplified: 我的父母很早就跟我说过，三大家族的孩子长大了都是要做官的。
sentences.traditional: 我的父母很早就跟我說過，三大家族的孩子長大了都是要做官的。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ de fù mǔ hěn zǎo jiù gēn wǒ shuō guò sān dà jiā zú de hái zi zhǎng dà le dōu shì yào zuò guān de
sentences.english: My parents had told me early on that the children of the three great families were all expected to become officials when they grew up.

sentences.simplified: 我收拾行李，离开了家乡。
sentences.traditional: 我收拾行李，離開了家鄉。
sentences.pinyin: wǒ shōu shi xíng li lí kāi le jiā xiāng
sentences.english: I packed my bags and left my hometown.

sentence_translations: Chapter 2: I Write “Ode to the Orange Tree”
I was born in 340 BC. I am from the state of Chu.
At that time, there were three great families in the state of Chu. They were the most powerful people in the state of Chu.
My family name is Qu, and the Qu family was one of these three great families.
I spent my childhood in a place called Lepingli.
The people there were very kind, the scenery was beautiful, and there were all kinds of lovely animals and plants.
I loved reading from a young age and read all kinds of books.
I often walked among the mountains and rivers with a book in hand, reading as I observed the interesting plants and animals.
Sometimes I would meet people going out to work in the fields, ..
.. and they would smile and ask me whether it was the books that were interesting, or the flowers and plants that were interesting.
It was a happy childhood.
In my hometown, there was a sweet and juicy fruit called the orange.
Oranges only grew in the south, and you couldn’t find them outside the state of Chu.
I loved eating oranges since I was young, and there were many orange trees near my home.
I often read under the orange trees, and as I smelled their fragrance and that of the oranges, I felt that life was beautiful.
I wrote a poem for the orange, called “Ode to the Orange Tree”. In the poem, I wrote:
“Oh, beautiful tree growing between heaven and earth, born in the lands of the southern country.
Green leaves, white flowers—how adorable they are!
Rooted in the southern country, it grows between heaven and earth, never influenced by others.
I hope to grow with you and always be friends with you.
“Ode to the Orange Tree” was the first Chinese poem to use an object to express the poet’s aspirations, ..
.. and it was also how later generations started to get to know me.
Later generations said I was like the orange tree: I had a deep love for my country, and was honest and dedicated.
But to be honest, when I wrote the poem, I didn’t think that much, because I was still young and had not yet experienced hardship.
“Ode to the Orange Tree” spread to the capital of Chu—Yindu. The king living there read my poem and said that he liked it.
At the age of twenty, I received a notice from the king asking me to go to Yindu.
Yindu was the most important city in the state of Chu, and I went there to become an official.
Of course, my opportunity to become an official was not entirely because of “Ode to the Orange Tree”.
My parents had told me early on that the children of the three great families were all expected to become officials when they grew up.
I packed my bags and left my hometown.
